prompt: Customers earn one point per order and see their total points balance in the cart; you can view and manually adjust points in the admin.

intent.desiredOutcome: Customers earn one point per order and see their total points balance in the cart; you can view and manually adjust points in the admin.
intent.qualityBrief: A good version includes a clean admin list of customers sorted by points, with a quick-edit form to add or subtract points per customer. Key edge cases: handling guest checkouts (no points recorded), ensuring the cart widget updates after order completion, and validating manual adjustments to prevent negative points. UX detail: the admin should show order count per customer alongside points to help you understand earning patterns, and manual adjustments should log who made the change and when for audit purposes.

plan.dataFlow: When an order is completed, the system reads the order to confirm it is a non-guest, completed order and retrieves the customer identifier and completion status. If no award already exists for that order, the system appends a one-point ledger entry and increments the customer's running balance and order count; duplicate deliveries for the same order are no-ops. When a customer views their cart, the widget calls the app's balance endpoint and displays the stored point total. In the admin, a merchant lists customers sorted by points balance with pagination, and may submit a manual adjustment that appends an audited ledger entry and updates the customer's balance, subject to a non-negative balance invariant.

triggers.idempotency: if a points ledger entry for the same order identifier already exists, treat the event as a no-op and do not award additional points

capabilities.description: Fetch the completed order to confirm it is a non-guest order and retrieve the customer identifier needed to award points.
Determine whether a points ledger entry already exists for the given order to enforce idempotency.
Append a one-point earned entry to the customer's points ledger for the completed order.
Increment the customer's stored total points balance and lifetime order count after a points award.
Return the current points total for a specific customer so the cart widget can display it.
Return a paginated list of customers with their points balance and lifetime order count for the admin panel.
Record a merchant-initiated points adjustment in the ledger and update the customer's stored balance.

persistence.name: customer_points
persistence.purpose: Stores each customer's current points balance and lifetime order count as a single authoritative summary row.

columns.name: customer_external_id
columns.purpose: links this row to the customer in the external platform

persistence.keyedBy: one row per customer, keyed by the customer's external identifier
queryPatterns: single row lookup by customer external identifier for widget balance reads
full list ordered by points total descending with page-based offset for admin list
single row lookup by customer external identifier before and after a manual adjustment

persistence.name: points_ledger
persistence.purpose: Immutable append-only log of every points transaction — both order-earned awards and manual adjustments — for audit and idempotency.

externalContracts.purpose: Returns the current points balance for the authenticated customer so the cart widget can render it on page load.
Returns a paginated list of customers with their points balance and order count, sorted by points descending.
Applies a merchant-initiated points adjustment to a customer and records it in the audit ledger.

edgeCases: A guest checkout triggers an order-completed event but carries no customer identifier — the system must detect the guest flag and skip awarding points without creating a ledger entry.

The same order-completed event is delivered more than once — the system must detect the existing ledger entry for that order identifier and treat the duplicate as a no-op, leaving the balance unchanged.
A manual adjustment submitted in the admin would reduce a customer's points total below zero — the system must reject the adjustment and return a validation error before writing any records.

An order-completed event arrives before the customer summary row exists — the system must create the customer_points row as part of the same award operation to avoid a missing-row error on the balance update.

The cart widget is loaded immediately after an order completes, before the webhook has been processed — the widget must display the last-known persisted balance rather than inferring a real-time total, and no stale-read correction is required beyond eventual consistency.

hld_v_findings.issue: The signal field "order completion status" is declared on the external-event trigger but does not appear in the dataNeeds of any capability; every capability that handles the webhook uses only "order identifier" and "customer identifier", so the status field is never consumed and the plan gives LLD no guidance on how completion is verified from the event payload itself.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add "order completion status" to the dataNeeds of the read-completed-order capability (or remove it from signalFields if the status is always implied by the webhook topic), so the field is explicitly mapped to the step that validates the order before awarding points.

hld_v_findings.issue: This GET route returns a list ("customers") but its requestShape declares no page parameter and its responseShape declares no total-count field; a merchant with thousands of customers will receive an unbounded result set with no way to paginate, making the admin list unusable at scale.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a page (or cursor) parameter to requestShape and a total_count field to responseShape, and document the per-page limit so LLD can implement pagination from the start.

hld_v_findings.issue: This GET route returns a list ("entries") but declares no page parameter in requestShape and no entry count in responseShape; a high-volume customer's ledger will grow unbounded and the endpoint will have no pagination contract for LLD to implement.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a page (or cursor) parameter to requestShape and an entry_count (or total_entries) field to responseShape consistent with the pattern used on the customers-list endpoint.
